newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Rank selling Xerox stake for one bln pounds.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Rank selling Xerox stake for one bln pounds.

text.p: Shares in Rank Group Plc rose over five percent on Friday after it agreed to sell its 20 percent stake in office equipment venture Rank Xerox for up to one billion pounds ($1.6 billion).
Rank has signed an initial agreement to sell the stake to Xerox Corporation of the U.S., giving Xerox full ownership of a joint venture set up over 40 years ago.

Xerox will pay an initial sum 500 million pounds on completion, expected later this month. Two annual instalments of 220 million pounds will follow plus a further payment of 60 million dependent on profits.
Leisure and entertainment company Rank said it would use part of the proceeds to repurchase up to 250 million pounds worth of its own shares.
"I'm very pleased with the price and it (the deal) is earlier than we expected," Rank chief executive Andrew Teare told Reuters.
"This had to be dealt with before we moved forward. It didn't fit into our product portfolio and we didn't manage it," he added.
The stock market gave the deal and planned repurchase the thumbs-up, Rank shares adding 27p to close at 449.5p.
"The key thing is the timing. I don't think anyone really expected this to happen until the end of the year," said one share analyst.
The Rank Xerox joint venture dates back to 1956. Based in the southern English town of Marlow, it manufactures and markets Xerox products to more than 80 nations around the globe.
Xerox Corporation paid 620 million pounds for 40 percent of Rank's stake in the venture in February 1995.

Teare, who became chief executive in April 1996, is in the process of reshaping Rank, which owns and operates the Hard Rock cafes around the world and owns a range of bars, cinemas and nightclubs in Britain.
The company has raised some 1.3 billion pounds in disposals over the past year or so, Friday's deal being by far the largest.

Rank said it would use the remainder of the proceeds after the buyback to cut debt and invest in its businesses. Teare said he would seek small acquisitions as bigger deals in the sector were too expensive.
Rank is expanding its existing businesses aggressively, pledging to pump 1.5 billion pounds into UK leisure sites over the next four or five years.
It also plans to open new Hard Rock cafes around the world at the rate of one per month over the next three years. REUTER KPW
